The evidence splits each board's co-existing rows into per-identity **series** (see the split note below) and reports whether each one `moved` or is `frozen` over `duplicates_lookback_days` (default 7). `verdict` is DESCRIPTIVE and never asserts which identity is the real player (nothing in the data supports that): `one_live` (exactly one series still moving, the rest frozen - what a leftover leaderboard row looks like), `multi_live` (2+ still moving - separate active identities sharing a name), `all_idle` (nothing moved in the window, undecidable), `case_only`, `not_analysed` (dated by the archive backfill but never measured - it only reads the series for names still in the newest capture, since an older window is cold-tiered and costs ~35s apiece; `evidence` is `{}` and this is NOT a finding of "nothing moved"). Detected **live** by the leaderboards warmer on the newest capture each ingest, and datable across the whole archive via the master backfill below. Records persist in a `player_duplicate` table (one row per name); gated by the `feature_leaderboard_duplicates_enabled` master switch (OFF → 404 here and `enabled:false` on the `/site` proxy). Knobs: `duplicates_*` (master panel, `duplicates` category). `Cache-Control: public, max-age=duplicates_cache_ttl_seconds` (default 300).
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/duplicates/{name}` → `{ query, found, enabled, name, kind, verdict, boards, max_occurrences, spellings, first_anchor, last_anchor, evidence, method_version, updated_at }` - **tokenless**. Whether ONE name resolves to more than one identity, case-insensitive. `found:false` is the normal answer and means the name is unambiguous. When true, treat that player's LIFETIME aggregate (best rank, appearances, totals) as covering more than one identity - the per-board evidence separates the score lines, but the aggregate cannot be split retroactively.
- `POST /v1/leaderboards/duplicates-backfill[?clear_first=false]` - **master only**. Walk EVERY stored capture and (re)detect duplicated names into `player_duplicate`, folding each anchor into the record so `first_anchor` dates the real start of the duplication (the live pass only ever sees the newest capture, so it can't). Idempotent; `clear_first=true` wipes first. Returns **202**, runs in the BACKGROUND (single-flight guarded). Poll `GET /v1/leaderboards/duplicates-backfill-status` → `{ running, total, done, detected, last_anchor, recorded_duplicates, … }`. NOTE: `case` groups are captured at ingest from the raw dump, so this rebuilds `same_name` groups only - a `clear_first` run drops case history until new captures land or the backlog is re-ingested.
- **Per-identity series split (applies everywhere, not gated by the flag).** Because a duplicated name has two rows at the SAME anchor on the same board, any naive per-player read interleaves two people: the chart drew both values at each timestamp as one vertical sawtooth, and day-over-day deltas compared a row against the other identity's previous value (producing multi-million-point phantom gains). `GET /v1/leaderboards/players/{name}/series` now emits **one entry per identity** - each carries `slot` (0-based, stable, ordered by first appearance) and `slots` (how many identities that board resolved to), with `duplicate_boards` on the payload - and `…/history` rows carry the same `slot`/`slots`. Rows are linked capture-to-capture by score continuity: each open series predicts its next value from its own recent rate and the assignment minimising total miss wins, with score DROPS penalised. Sorting by score was rejected (a frozen leftover row can sit ABOVE the live one, so the lines swap when the live one overtakes it), as was minimising raw score movement (degenerate - when every row rises, total movement is identical for every pairing). `slots` is 1 for every unambiguous player, so existing consumers are unaffected. The profile's `last_played` is likewise computed per slot; without it the lag alternated between the two rows and the player read as permanently active.
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/records` → `{ trove_mastery, geode_mastery, power_rank }` - **tokenless**. The current in-game *ceiling* for each stat, read off the rank-1 holder of the relevant **lifetime** board (these never reset, so their #1 is an all-time record). `trove_mastery` (board 1) and `geode_mastery` (board 20) are `{ points, level, points_into_level, points_to_next_level, player_name, anchor }` - the boards store a running Mastery **points** total, and `level` runs that total through the in-game points→level curve (levels 2-5 cost 25pts, 6-10 cost 50, 11-20 cost 75, 21-300 cost 100, 301+ cost `150 + ceil((level-300)*0.5)`), with `points_into_level`/`points_to_next_level` showing progress into the current level. **Geode is soft-capped at level 100 in-game**, so its `level` is clamped there and it carries extra fields `{ level_cap: 100, uncapped_level, capped }` - `uncapped_level` is what the points would reach without the cap (e.g. `100` vs a true `143`), `capped=true` when the two differ. `power_rank` is `{ value, board_uuid, player_name, anchor }` - the single highest Power Rank across all 17 per-class boards (1000-1016); `value` is stored directly (no level conversion) and `board_uuid` says which class board it came from. Any of the three is `null` only if that board has never been ingested. Refreshes at most once per daily dump (11:00 UTC); `Cache-Control: public, max-age=900`.
- `POST /v1/leaderboards/insert[?timestamp=<unix>]` (multipart `file`) - **master only**. Submit the raw cfg text as a multipart `file` field. Idempotent for a given anchor: re-running the same dump on the same timestamp converges. `timestamp` is optional and only used for back-fills; omit it for a normal scrape. Returns **202 Accepted** immediately with `{ accepted, bytes, message }` - the parse + persist (sub-second `COPY` load on a full dump) runs in the BACKGROUND so the bot's client isn't held open and timed out; the resulting `{ boards, entries, cleared_before_insert, created_at }` counts (or any parse/DB error, as `success:false`) are written to the master ingest log when processing finishes. **Full-history storage in PostgreSQL** (a dedicated DB, separate from the app's Mongo): the `entry` table is RANGE-partitioned by anchor (one partition per trove-day, 11:00-UTC boundary), so old data is just old partitions - no hot/cold collection split. Partitioned-parent indexes `(board_uuid, anchor, rank)` and `(player_id, anchor)` keep both board-at-time and player-over-time reads O(index seek) at any age; player names are normalised into a `player` dimension table. `leaderboards_hot_retention_days` (default 3 days; runtime-tunable from the master admin panel) now just controls how many recent days the warmer pre-warms / the page surfaces. Use `/timestamps?limit=` to enumerate ALL stored anchors (deduped). **Archive rate limit**: queries with a `?created_at=` older than `leaderboards_archive_query_threshold_days` (default 3 - bot captures hourly, so a 3-day window already covers ~72 anchors of "recent" data) pay a SECOND, tighter per-token bucket (default 10 req/min) on top of the standard cap - surfaced via `X-RateLimit-Archive-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset` response headers. Applies to `/v1/leaderboards?created_at=` and `/v1/leaderboards/{uuid}/entries?created_at=`; queries within the threshold pay only the standard cap. The threshold is runtime-tunable from the master admin panel. **Ingest cooldown**: API-token submissions are additionally capped at `ingest_cooldown_max` per `ingest_cooldown_window_seconds` (default 1 per 300s) per token per endpoint - exceeding returns 429 with `Retry-After`. Session-JWT calls (portal "Manual cfg ingest") bypass this so master back-fills aren't blocked. **Completeness guard**: a LIVE capture is REJECTED (not stored, ack'd but flagged `success:false` in the ingest log with the reason) when it arrives materially incomplete vs the previous good capture - the in-game scrape can return a short dump when the leaderboards are briefly down or crash mid-run. Detection is by board PRESENCE (id set): reject when more than `capture_max_missing_boards` (default 1) boards present last capture are absent now, or (secondary) when a board present in both COLLAPSED below `capture_collapse_frac` (default 0.5) of its previous entry count. Gated to non-reset windows (board rotation / daily zeroing at a reset is legitimate) and skipped when the previous capture had < `capture_min_prev_boards` boards. Rejecting is deliberate: storing a short dump poisons every delta consumer (activity, cheater velocity, renames, day-over-day deltas) because players merely absent from it read as "newly appeared / active"; dropping it makes the hour a clean time-gap that all of them already bridge over. The raw dump is still saved to the backlog for audit / manual re-ingest. The guard is SKIPPED on `?backfill=true` bulk re-seeds (trusts the operator). All knobs (`capture_completeness_enabled`, `capture_max_missing_boards`, `capture_collapse_frac`, `capture_min_prev_boards`) are runtime-tunable (master panel, `ingest_quality` category).
- `POST /v1/leaderboards/delete-anchor?anchor=<unix>[&recompute=true]` - **master only**. Delete every entry for ONE capture - purge a bad capture that slipped in before the guard (or was force-ingested). The hour becomes a clean time-gap that activity / cheater / rename / delta calculations bridge over. With `recompute` (default) the activity history is rebuilt in the background (the affected window recomputes as a gap, so any spike it caused disappears) and the leaderboards warmer is kicked. Returns `{ deleted, anchor, entries_deleted, recompute }`.

### Activity (`activity:read`) - free/public Trove player-activity estimates

Lower-bound active-player counts derived from the leaderboard captures (distinct top-N players whose score rose between captures). **Public / tokenless** - a token carrying `activity:read` just earns the wider per-token budget. Powers the showcase `/activity` ("Player Activity") page via the same-origin `/site` proxies, but documented + stable for third-party dashboards / wikis too. All cached for `cheaters_cache_ttl_seconds`. (These replaced the old `/v1/misc/activity*` and `/v1/leaderboards/activity*` copies.)
- `GET /v1/activity/current` → `{ estimate, estimate_24h, estimate_7d, window_24h_start, window_7d_start, span_24h_hours, span_7d_hours, window_start, window_end, duration_hours, by_board:[{uuid,name,category,active_players}], boards_analyzed, methodology, computed_at }` - lower-bound distinct active players between the two most recent captures: a player whose score ROSE on any board vs the previous capture, or who newly appears with a non-zero score (`score > prev`, absent-previous treated as 0). No score ceilings, no board filters; a reset drop isn't a rise. `estimate_24h` / `estimate_7d` are distinct-active rollups over the last 24h / 7d - the distinct UNION of each capture's active set in the period. Each capture's set is MATERIALIZED once in an `activity_active` table, so the rollups are an indexed `COUNT(DISTINCT)` over the windows in range - the true union, MONOTONIC (`7d ⊇ 24h ⊇ 1h`), no re-scan. `null` until an earlier anchor exists; `span_*_hours` = the window actually covered. `estimate` is `null` until two captures exist.
- `GET /v1/activity/history?days=7` (1–30) → `{ days, window_start, window_end, methodology, points:[{window_end, window_start, duration_hours, estimate, estimate_per_hour}] }` - time-series, one point per consecutive capture pair. `estimate_per_hour = estimate / duration_hours` is the value a chart should plot (a missed capture makes a window span 2-3h and inflates the raw `estimate`; the per-hour rate normalises it). Persisted per ingest, survives restarts.
- `GET /v1/activity/series?period=7d` (period ∈ `1d`/`7d`/`1m` - longer ranges were removed) → `{ period, bucket_seconds, window_start, window_end, points:[{t, active, avg, peak, samples}], peak:{t, active}|null, low:{t, active}|null, average, latest, methodology }` - downsampled activity-level series; each point is a fixed time bucket sized to the period (hourly for `1d`/`7d`, daily for `1m`). `active` is the plotted value with EXTREMES PRESERVED: the single busiest bucket in the range plots its true max (at the exact peak capture), the single quietest its true min, every other bucket its `avg` - so a coarse wide-timeframe bucket never flattens the real peak into an average. `avg` is always the bucket mean; `peak` its busiest hour. Top-level `peak`/`low` are the period's true max/min (timestamped at the actual capture); `average`/`latest` summarise the period. Buckets whose windows span a missed capture are DROPPED, not zero-filled, so `points` can have holes - a renderer should judge contiguity on the bucket index (`floor(t / bucket_seconds)`, since `t` is the bucket's centroid/extreme, not its start) and draw the missing stretches dashed rather than as a straight climb. Backs the `/activity` page charts.
- `POST /v1/activity/backfill[?total_days=400&chunk_days=14&force=false&reset=false]` - **master only**. Seeds the `/series` history from the stored Postgres captures so the multi-period charts have data predating the hourly forward-fill. `total_days=0` rebuilds ALL stored history (no lower bound); else the trailing N days. Returns **202** + runs in the BACKGROUND, STREAMING one capture's entries at a time (a 1-deep sliding window over consecutive anchor pairs), so peak memory stays at ~one capture regardless of range - the naive "load the whole range into one dict" approach OOMs on dense hourly data. Coverage capped by how far the stored entries reach; `force=false` skips already-computed windows. (`chunk_days` is accepted for compatibility but unused now that the load streams.) The per-hour series skips windows that span a missed capture; the gap cutoff is derived from the **median capture cadence** (not a hardcoded 1h), so a non-hourly or jittery archive isn't dropped wholesale - the backfill logs `median_interval_hours` / `gap_threshold_hours` / `gap_skipped` for diagnosis. **`reset=true` is destructive**: it first DELETES every stored estimate, then recomputes the whole range from scratch (implies `force`) - use it to flush miscalculations from older runs. The `activity_estimate` table is fully derived data, so nothing irreplaceable is lost; the charts just read empty until the rebuild lands (`reset_deleted` count is logged).

### Class activity (`activity:read`) - free/public per-class Trove activity

Per-Trove-class version of player activity, from the **Effort (`4000+i`)** leaderboards: `class_index = board_uuid % 1000` maps to the game's class release order (0=Knight … 17=Solarion, verified against the stored board names). Paragon (`5000+i`) is **excluded as ambiguous** — neither counted nor filtered on. A class is "active" in a window when a player's score rose (or first appears) on its Effort board (this score-rose measure drives the time-series `/series`; the donut `/current` instead counts players simply *present* on the Effort board in the latest snapshot — see each endpoint below). Effort boards reset weekly (Mon 11:00 UTC) so windows crossing the reset are unmeasurable (no point). **Two views in every payload:** RAW counts everyone; CLEAN (the `/class-activity` page default, "established", `*_clean` fields) keeps only players who, snapshot at the window end, clear ALL THREE floors — Power Rank (`1000+i` board) ≥ `class_activity_power_rank_threshold` (default **25000**), Effort (`4000+i`) ≥ `class_activity_effort_threshold` (default **50**) and score on the global XP stats board (`21005`) ≥ `class_activity_xp_threshold` (default **2,000,000**) — all three master-tunable runtime settings (set any to 0 to drop that gate); this filters new characters + alts. A player missing from a captured XP board reads as 0 (filtered, same as the other floors), but an XP board absent from a capture entirely degrades the XP floor to a no-op for that window (it never zeroes the clean view). `clean` is `null` where unmeasurable (no Power Rank snapshot). Same `activity:read` scope, same `/site/leaderboards/class-activity/*` proxy family, powers the `/class-activity` page (multi-line chart with an Established/All toggle + player-share donut).
- `GET /v1/class-activity/current` → `{ window_start, window_end, duration_hours, total_active, total_active_clean, total_effort_added, total_effort_added_clean, power_rank_threshold, effort_threshold, xp_threshold, classes:[{class_index, name, icon, active_players, share, active_players_clean, share_clean, effort_added, effort_added_clean}], methodology, computed_at }` - **a direct headcount of the LATEST snapshot, NOT the activity pipeline**: per class, the players *present* on its Effort board at the newest capture (Paragon excluded; no score-rose step), for BOTH views (`share`/`share_clean` each sum to 1 over their measurable classes). `effort_added`/`effort_added_clean` (+ the `total_*` rollups) are the Effort added to each board in the **latest hour** (this capture vs the previous; Σ positive per-player gains, per view; `null` when there's no previous capture or the pair crosses the weekly reset). `share` is share-of-players: a player on N classes counts in each, NOT distinct players. `*_clean` is `null` where the clean view is unmeasurable (no Power Rank board in the snapshot). `window_start`=`window_end`=snapshot anchor; `duration_hours` is null. `classes` sorted by the clean view desc (None last). (Powers the page's player-share donut; `/series` below stays activity-based.)
- `GET /v1/class-activity/series?period=7d` (period ∈ `1d`…`all`) → `{ period, bucket_seconds, window_start, window_end, power_rank_threshold, effort_threshold, xp_threshold, buckets:[t,…], classes:[{class_index, name, icon, values:[float|null,…], values_clean:[float|null,…]}], methodology }` - per-class bucketed series with a SHARED x-axis (`buckets`); each class's `values` (raw) and `values_clean` (PR+Effort+XP-filtered) align to it (avg active/hr per bucket on the Effort board, `null` where that view had no measurable window in the bucket). Peak-preserving like `/v1/activity/series`: each class's busiest bucket plots its true max instead of the bucket average, so a coarse wide-timeframe bucket still shows the real peak (short ranges are unchanged; only the peak is preserved per class, not the min). Same bucket sizing as `/v1/activity/series`. **Two kinds of hole** a renderer must not draw through: a `null` in a class's `values` (that view had no measurable window there - e.g. a window crossing the weekly reset), and a bucket missing from `buckets` entirely (no captures at all). Both are caught by judging contiguity on the bucket key (`floor(bucket_t / bucket_seconds)`, since `buckets` carries centroids) and stroking the missing stretch dashed rather than as a straight rise.
- `POST /v1/class-activity/backfill[?total_days=400&force=false&reset=false]` - **master only**. Seeds the per-class history (raw + clean; `class_activity_estimate` table) from stored captures; same memory-safe streaming as the activity backfill, loading the 18 Effort boards + 18 Power Rank boards (+ the XP board `21005` when that floor is on) per anchor. `total_days=0` = all history; `reset=true` wipes first (implies force). **202** + background. Run after changing any clean-view floor to apply it across history (the warmer applies it to the latest window each capture automatically).

### Giveaways (`giveaways:read`) - free/public Trove community giveaways

**Public / tokenless** - a token carrying `giveaways:read` just earns the wider per-token budget. The showcase `/giveaways` page is the main consumer (via the same-origin `/site/giveaways` proxy); this is the documented, stable API surface. (Entering a giveaway is a signed-in site-user action, not part of the public API.)
- `GET /v1/giveaways/ongoing` → `[{ id, title, description, prize_name, status, starts_at, ends_at, entry_count, winner_username }]` - currently-OPEN giveaways (accepting entries), soonest to end first. `status` is `"open"` for all of these; `winner_username` is always `null` (winners only appear after a draw) and the prize code is NEVER exposed. Use `entry_count` to compute odds (`1 / entry_count`) and `ends_at` for the countdown. Cached 30s.
- `GET /v1/giveaways/upcoming` → same shape - SCHEDULED giveaways not yet open, soonest-starting first. `status` is `"scheduled"`; `entry_count` is 0 until `starts_at`. Cached 30s.
- `GET /v1/giveaways/ended[?days=7]` (days 1–30) → same shape - giveaways that ENDED in the last `days` days (default 7), most-recently-ended first. `status` is `"drawn"` (had a winner - see `winner_username`) or `"closed"` (no entrants); cancelled giveaways are excluded. Cached 30s.

### Market (`market:read`) - Trove marketplace listings

Ingested from the same bot that submits leaderboards. Every hour or so the bot reads the game's `GrainusMod.cfg` and POSTs the raw text to `/v1/market/insert`. Each line is `<uuid>;<name>;<type>;<stack>;<price>` with the UUID v1 of the in-game listing. Listings are stored in **Postgres** (`market_listing` table, the same DB as leaderboards): the UUID is the primary key, its timestamp decodes into `created_at` (when the player posted the listing), and `last_seen` is bumped on every re-scrape via UPSERT (so re-seeing the same listing never duplicates). Only items on the interest list (`gamedata/market_items.json`) are persisted - anything else is dropped at ingest. Listings expire 7 days after `created_at` OR after 3 hours with no re-scrape; `hide_expired=true` (default on reads) filters those out. `item_summary` computes an exact median via `percentile_cont`. `/insert` is **master-only**.
- `GET /v1/market/listings[?name=&price_min=&price_max=&last_seen_after=&hide_expired=true&sort=-last_seen&limit=100&offset=0]` → `{ items: [Listing], count, total }`, Listing = `{ id, name, type, stack, price, price_each, last_seen, created_at, expires_at, expired }`. Default sort newest-`last_seen` first; pass `+price_each` to sort cheapest-first. `id` is the game's UUID v1 stringified. **Archive rate limit**: passing `hide_expired=false` (asking for expired/historical listings) pays a SECOND, tighter per-token bucket (default 10 req/min) on top of the standard cap - surfaced via `X-RateLimit-Archive-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset` response headers. The default `hide_expired=true` pays only the standard cap. (Market doesn't need a "90-day" threshold like leaderboards; the in-game 7-day listing lifetime already defines fresh-vs-historical, so the archive limit fires on the opt-in flag instead of an anchor age.)
- `GET /v1/market/items` → `{ items: [<name>], count }` - item names with at least one stored listing (sorted). (The `/market` **site page** additionally decorates each item with a thumbnail: it reverses the listing's display name back to a codex entry to recover its `blueprint`, then renders it via `/v1/codexes/render`. When a name sits on several prefab roles (e.g. a piñata's item token vs its mount body) the tradable item's icon wins; a name with no codex entry, or whose top role still disagrees on the blueprint, shows no thumbnail - a wrong image is worse than none. Site-only, via the `/site/market/item-images` proxy; there is no v1 item→image endpoint.)
- For the bot's scan allow-list see `GET /v1/misc/interest-items` (moved out of market - it's tokenless so dashboards / wikis can fetch it without a key). Admin-managed via `/admin/market/interest-items` (master panel). The `/market` sidebar's collapsible item groups come from the admin-defined categories (`/admin/market/categories`, master panel; Mongo `market_item_categories`); membership is by item name so allow-list churn (deletes, bulk replace) never uncategorizes.
- `GET /v1/market/items/{name}/summary` → `{ name, count, total_price, total_stack, min_each, max_each, avg_each, median_each }` - aggregate stats across active (non-expired) listings of one item. 404 when no active listings exist.
- `POST /v1/market/insert[?timestamp=<unix>]` (multipart `file`) - **master only**. Submit the raw cfg text. Returns `{ parsed, imported, ignored_not_in_list, last_seen }`. `timestamp` overrides the `last_seen` anchor (only for back-fills). Listings are upserted by UUID - same listing re-scraped bumps `last_seen`, never duplicates. **Ingest cooldown**: same per-token, per-endpoint cap as `/v1/leaderboards/insert` (default 1 per 300s; API-token only; session-JWT replay through the portal bypasses).
- `POST /v1/market/reset` - **master only. Destructive.** TRUNCATEs the whole `market_listing` table (active + historical) and returns `{ reset: true, removed: <prior row count> }`. The interest-items allow-list is kept. Use it to clear seed/demo data before the live hourly scrape takes over. Also surfaced as a danger-zone button in the dev-portal ingest panel.
- **Listing fee and sale tax are not part of the API** - no endpoint returns them and no field carries them. They are a published *game* constant, computed client-side on the `/market` page (`site/static/market-fees.js`, exported as `window.BTTMarketFee`) for the Fees tab and for the **Fee** / **Seller nets** columns on each listing row. The fee is a cubic Bézier over control points `(50, 1500, 6000, 65000)` in `t = (min(price, 40_000_000) - 1) / (40_000_000 - 1)`, **truncated**: `fee(t) = 50(1-t)³ + 3·1500·t(1-t)² + 3·6000·t²(1-t) + 65000·t³`. Samples: 15k→51, 250k→77, 1M→165, 10M→2513, 25M→18904, 40M and above→65000 (flat). **40M is where the curve reaches its 65,000 cap, not the maximum listable price.** The fee is charged per *listing* (on its total price, not per item in the stack) at posting time; a sale refunds it and takes a 10% tax (seller nets `price × 0.90`), while an expired listing keeps no tax but loses the fee.

### Store (`store:read`) - the in-game Kiwi Store catalog

Ingested from a scraper tmod (StoreLog) that replaces `ui/kiwistore.swf`: it records everything the game engine pushes into the store window (tabs, product tiles, prices, sale stickers, limited-time-deal countdowns, class tiles, texture layers, lootbox probability text), walks every tab, and dumps it into its mod cfg; the bot POSTs that cfg to `/v1/store/insert`. Products are upserted by their **engine product code** (stable key); a price-history point is appended only when the price signature actually changes, so sales and price bumps are queryable over time. Each ingest also records **availability intervals** (present-in-store runs) so an accurate day-by-day timeline is queryable, and a product missing from the latest scrape is never deleted - it just goes `active:false` (delisted) and keeps its history. A same-origin website view of all this lives at **`/store`** (Trove Store History: a pack gallery with in-game art + a global availability timeline; in-game `.dds` textures are served from the updates CAS and decoded client-side). Prices are in-game currencies (`TWC` credits / `TWP` cubits, with patron `monthly` pricing and `sale` sticker keys); real-money SKUs carry a pre-formatted `price_string` instead. Names/labels are the game's raw localization keys (e.g. `$Store_...`) exactly as the engine sent them. `/insert` and `/reset` are **master-only**.
- `GET /v1/store/products[?category=&kind=&currency=&q=&active=true&on_sale=false&limit=100&offset=0]` → `{ items: [Product], count, total, anchor }`. Product = `{ code, kind, name, image, info, informational, tradable, prices: [{currency, cost, can_purchase, monthly, sale}], price_string, price_string_currency, price_string_sale, promo, deal_expires_at, interact_label, interact_enabled, trial_limits, class_level, class_power_rank, class_sub_name, class_icon, textures, loot_title, loot_body, categories, first_seen, last_seen, active }`. `kind` ∈ `product|starter|patron|interactable|trial|class`; `active=false` includes delisted products; `on_sale=true` filters to products currently carrying a sale sticker; `anchor` is the latest ingest's unix-seconds timestamp.
- `GET /v1/store/categories` → `{ items: [{index, label, icon, codes, count, active}], count, anchor }` - the store's tab list with display-ordered product codes.
- `GET /v1/store/timeline[?kind=&limit=1000]` → `{ anchor, span:{start,end}, items: [{code, name, kind, image, availability, first_seen, last_seen, active}], count }` - **availability bands for every product in one call**. `availability` is `[[start,end], ...]` unix-second intervals - one per continuous run the product was in-store, so a pack that left and returned shows multiple bands (honest "when was this available", which `first_seen`/`last_seen` alone can't express). Ordered most-recently-present first; `span` gives the axis bounds. Drives the store-history timeline view.
- `GET /v1/store/products/{code}` → Product + `price_history: [{ts, prices, price_string}]` + `availability: [[start,end], ...]` + `records` - one price point per ingest where the price signature changed (sales starting/ending, price bumps, purchase-option swaps); `records` = `{times_available, returns, total_days_seen, longest_run_days, first_seen, last_seen, currently_active, gap_days, price_low:{cur:n}, price_high:{cur:n}, price_changes}` (derived at-a-glance stats). 404 for an unknown code.
- `POST /v1/store/insert[?timestamp=<unix>]` (multipart `file`) - **master only**. Submit the raw StoreLog.cfg text. Returns `{ products, categories, created, price_changes, anchor, done_marker }`. Idempotent per product; `timestamp` overrides the anchor (back-fills only). Publishes a `store` SSE event on success.
- `POST /v1/store/reset` - **master only. Destructive.** Wipes every stored product/category + the ingest state (bad-ingest escape hatch); returns `{ reset: true, removed }`.

### OCR (`ocr:read`) - read character stats from a screenshot (self-hosted)

Self-hosted OCR (RapidOCR / ONNX - **no external service, no LLM**) that reads the in-game character stat sheet from a screenshot. The UI is moddable (themes, fonts, columns, language), so this doesn't trust raw OCR text: every recognized label is fuzzy-matched against a CLOSED multilingual vocabulary (English + French) so a garbled or translated label still resolves to the right stat, and every value is sanity-checked against the stat's expected type (integer vs percent) + plausible range. **Token required** (not tokenless): the OCR model is CPU-heavy, so it's gated behind `ocr:read` rather than the per-IP anon budget. The image is processed in memory and never stored.
- `POST /v1/ocr/character` (multipart `file`; PNG / JPEG / WebP / GIF / BMP, ≤12 MB) → `{ stats: { <key>: { value, unit, raw, confidence, in_range, type_match, derived } }, matched, total_known, lines }`. `stats` is keyed by canonical stat key (`physical_damage`, `magic_damage`, `maximum_health`, `critical_hit`, `critical_damage`, `power_rank`, …). `value` is an integer for count stats and a float for percent stats; `unit` ∈ `count`/`percent`; `raw` is the number exactly as OCR read it (empty when derived); `confidence` (0-1) folds label-match quality with the validation result; `in_range`/`type_match` flag a value that parsed but looks implausible for that stat (don't trust a stat with either `false`). `derived` is `true` when a value was COMPUTED rather than read: **`coefficient`** often isn't shown on the sheet, so it's derived as `floor(max(physical_damage, magic_damage) * (1 + critical_damage/100))` (the game's own formula) from those reads; when coefficient IS shown and agrees it's a confirmed read (`derived:false`), and a shown value that contradicts the formula is surfaced but flagged with low `confidence`. `matched` = how many known stats are present, `total_known` = vocabulary size, `lines` = the raw OCR text lines (transparency). Returns **503** (`service_unavailable`) if the OCR engine isn't installed on the server, **400** on an unreadable/empty image.

## Meta

- `GET /health` → `{ "status": "ok" }`
- `GET /openapi.json` → full machine-readable OpenAPI spec

## Example

```bash
export KIWI_TOKEN="kiwi_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"   # created in the portal

curl https://api.aallyn.net/v1/rotations/server-time \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KIWI_TOKEN"
```
